items.followUp: What are valence electrons? Name the two main types of chemical bond.

rubric.why: This identifies which electrons are bonding electrons and their role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bonding electrons are valence electrons involved in forming chemical bonds.

rubric.why: These are the two main types of chemical bond expected.
rubric.description: Names the types of chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both ionic and covalent bonds.

modelAnswer: Bonding electrons are the valence electrons that take part in forming chemical bonds.
The two main types of chemical bond are ionic (electrovalent) and covalent bonds.

items.followUp: Define intermolecular forces and identify two such forces between water molecules.

rubric.why: This states what intermolecular forces are and where they act.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining them as forces of attraction between molecules.

rubric.why: HCl molecules experience dipole–dipole attractions and London dispersion forces.
rubric.description: Identifies two intermolecular forces between HCl molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both dipole–dipole and London dispersion forces.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction between molecules.
Between HCl molecules, dipole–dipole attraction occurs: Hδ+···Clδ−.
London dispersion forces also act between HCl molecules.

items.followUp: Define boiling point and state the boiling point of water at standard atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: This is the defining condition for boiling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that boiling occurs when a liquid's vapour pressure equals atmospheric pressure.

rubric.description: States the boiling point of alcohol.

modelAnswer: The boiling point is the temperature at which a liquid's vapour pressure becomes equal to atmospheric pressure.
The boiling point of ethyl alcohol (ethanol) is 78°C (about 351 K).

items.followUp: Define allotropy and give one allotrope of phosphorus.

rubric.why: Allotropy describes the existence of an element in different forms in the same physical state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an element exists in different forms in the same physical state.

rubric.why: Diamond and graphite are different allotropes of carbon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as diamond or graphite.

modelAnswer: Allotropy is the property of an element to exist in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
For example, carbon exists as diamond and graphite.

items.followUp: Write and balance the chemical equation for the reaction of magnesium with oxygen.

rubric.why: Sodium is correctly included as a reactant in the reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing sodium and oxygen as reactants.

rubric.why: Sodium reacts with oxygen to form sodium oxide; the equation should be balanced.
rubric.description: Writes the product and balanced equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation 4Na + O₂ → 2Na₂O.

modelAnswer: Sodium reacts with oxygen to form sodium oxide.

items.followUp: What is dilution? Explain how adding water affects the concentration of a solution.

rubric.why: Adding solvent is the process used to dilute a solution.
rubric.description: States how a solution is diluted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that dilution is done by adding solvent.

rubric.why: Adding solvent increases the solution's volume without increasing the amount of solute, so its concentration decreases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that dilution decreases the concentration of a solution.

modelAnswer: Dilution is the process of decreasing the concentration of a solution by adding more solvent.
The amount of solute remains the same while the solution becomes less concentrated.

items.followUp: Define percentage mass by mass concentration and write its formula.

rubric.why: Percentage mass/volume expresses grams of solute in each 100 mL of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the mass in grams of solute dissolved in 100 mL of solution.

rubric.why: This gives the standard mass/volume percentage formula.
rubric.description: Gives the formula for percentage mass/volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula: % m/v = (mass of solute in g ÷ volume of solution in mL) × 100.

modelAnswer: Percentage mass/volume is the number of grams of solute dissolved in 100 mL of solution.
% m/v = (mass of solute in g ÷ volume of solution in mL) × 100.

items.followUp: Why does oil not dissolve in water? Use the terms polar and non-polar in your answer.

rubric.why: Ether, benzene and petrol are non-polar substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ether, benzene and petrol are non-polar.

rubric.why: Polar water does not dissolve these non-polar substances well; substances with similar polarity dissolve one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that water is polar and, because like dissolves like, the non-polar substances are insoluble in it.

modelAnswer: Ether, benzene and petrol are non-polar, whereas water is polar.
They are insoluble in water because like dissolves like; polar water does not dissolve non-polar substances.
